name: std/system
description: The host a program runs on: files, the trap handler and its stack traces, the dynamic loader and the object file it reads, the command interpreter and the standard streams, and what a process can say about itself.
residual: Split out of std/runtime 2026-08-16. These are the modules that used to be called runtime and are not: every one of them imports the library (Traps -> Streams, Loader -> Files, Commands -> Modules + Streams), so they sit above std/base rather than below it.

Traps, Reflection and TrapWriters are one family and the trap handler is arguably runtime -- Go puts panic and the traceback in its runtime. Ours cannot: it prints through Streams. Left here rather than given a special case.
